title: Ultralow-Field Triplon Condensation in a Spin-Ladder Magnet
authors: Ankit Labh, Ross H. Colman, Jakub Šebesta, Noah Oefele, Elsa Lhotel, Adam Berlie, Paul Steffens, Oksana Zaharko, Pascal Manuel, Iurii Kibalin, Philipp Gegenwart, Dominik Legut, Johanna K. Jochum, Alexander A. Tsirlin, Petr Čermák
abstract: We realise the first ultralow-field Bose-Einstein condensation of triplons in a spin-ladder magnet, uncovering a quantum critical point at only $μ_0 H_{c1}=0.17$ T in Henmilite ($\mathrm{Ca_2Cu(OH)_4[B(OH)_4]_2}$). Unlike dimer magnets, a ladder retains extended one-dimensional correlations in its gapped parent state, making this limit strongly fluctuation dominated. Thermodynamic, magnetoelastic, $μ$SR, and neutron-diffraction measurements overturn the previous assignment of zero-field antiferromagnetic order, establishing a quantum-disordered coupled-ladder parent state with persistent low-energy dynamics. The weak low-temperature anomaly instead marks a gap-controlled crossover from the correlated ladder regime into the activated quantum-disordered state. These measurements further reveal an exceptionally asymmetric ordered dome extending to $μ_0 H_{c2}\simeq 8.2$ T. Quantum Monte Carlo simulations for the relevant spin Hamiltonian place Henmilite just on the gapped side of the zero-field ladder-ordering instability, naturally accounting for the strong separation between the exchange and residual-gap scales and the tiny critical field. Our findings extend ultralow-field triplon condensation beyond the dimer paradigm and establish Henmilite as a platform for controlled tuning across quantum criticality in a fluctuation-dominated spin ladder.
summary: This paper reports the first observation of ultralow-field Bose-Einstein condensation of triplons in the spin-ladder magnet Henmilite. By combining advanced measurements with QMC simulations, the authors establish that the material resides in a quantum-disordered parent state, extending the BEC concept beyond simpler dimer magnets. This work provides a crucial platform for tuning and studying quantum criticality in fluctuation-dominated magnetic systems.
main_problem: The study aims to realize and characterize the ultralow-field Bose-Einstein condensation (BEC) of triplons in a spin-ladder magnet, extending the phenomenon beyond the established dimer magnet paradigm.
main_result: The authors report the first observation of BEC at an ultralow critical field ($\mu_0H_{c1} = 0.17 	ext{ T}$) in Henmilite, establishing the material as a platform for studying quantum criticality in a fluctuation-dominated spin ladder.
method: The research combines multiple experimental techniques (thermodynamic, $\mu	ext{SR}$, neutron diffraction) with advanced theoretical modeling, including Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations and Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations.
model_or_system: The physical system is Henmilite ($	ext{Ca}_2	ext{Cu}(	ext{OH})_4[	ext{B}(	ext{OH})_4]_2$), modeled as a coupled spin-ladder magnet governed by exchange couplings ($J_{	ext{leg}}, J_{	ext{rung}}, J_{	ext{inter}}$). The theoretical framework utilizes the BEC description for triplon condensation.
key_observables: Low-field critical fields ($\mu_0H_{c1} = 0.17 	ext{ T}$), the upper critical field ($\mu_0H_{c2} \simeq 8.2 	ext{ T}$), magnetic susceptibility, specific heat, and the asymmetry ratio ($m^*/m$).
important_parameters: The system is characterized by a strong separation between the exchange scale ($J \sim 3-4 	ext{ K}$) and the residual gap scale ($\Delta/k_B \simeq 0.245 	ext{ K}$), placing it near a quantum-disordered parent state.
main_assumptions: The BEC description assumes small symmetry-breaking terms, and the analysis relies on fitting the system to a coupled-ladder Hamiltonian derived from DFT and QMC simulations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the phase diagram showing BEC and correlated regimes, compare zero-field gaps vs. critical fields, and show the magnetic response ($	ext{M}/\mu_0	ext{H}$ and $	ext{C}_{	ext{mag}}/	ext{T}$) across different fields and temperatures.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first characterizing the parent state (overturning previous order assignments), then measuring the low-field anomaly using multiple probes, establishing the BEC regime, and finally using QMC/DFT to model the underlying spin Hamiltonian and explain the observed critical behavior.
why_interesting: The work provides a concrete, measurable realization of quantum criticality in a highly correlated magnetic material, using BEC theory to describe the transition, which is relevant to understanding quantum phase transitions in lattice models.
